why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
API keys, roles and the audit log are in. `npm test` passes (29 tests) and lint is clean. `data/db.json` has no keys, so it needs some before the server will accept requests.

- **Auth:** each request is checked before routing. A missing or unknown key gets `unauthorized` (401), and a known key without permission gets `forbidden` (403). Both use the usual error shape, with English messages (no Korean added).
- **Roles:** `viewer` can only GET. `cook` can also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. I read "enter counts" literally, so starting and finishing a stock-take are manager-only. `manager` can do everything, and `GET /audit` is manager-only.
- **Audit:** every non-GET request from a valid key appends `{at, name, method, path, status}` to `audit`. That includes requests that fail with a 4xx, such as a 409. A 403 is not logged, since nothing was attempted. `GET /audit` returns the entries newest first.
- **Schema:** adding `apiKeys` and `audit` counts as a schema change, so I bumped to schema 3 with a migration from 2. `data/seed.json` now has three keys, one per role (`viewer-key-1`, `cook-key-1`, `manager-key-1`).
- **Docs:** `README.md`, `docs/API.md`, `docs/DATA.md` and the `CHANGELOG.md` Unreleased section are updated.
- **Tests:** the shared `app()` helper in `tests/helpers.js` now sends the manager key by default, so the existing tests send a key without edits. I added `tests/auth.test.js` for 401, 403 and the audit log. I also changed `tests/cli.test.js` from schema 2 to 3, because the version bump broke it.
- **`data/db.json`:** I left it alone. It migrates to schema 3 on load with no keys, so every request will get 401 until you add `apiKeys`.
